# P32.13 — Immutable release namespaces and specific public record routes

**Requirement ids:** SIG-FIND-001, SIG-FIND-002 (§55.5) ·
**ADR:** ADR-132 ·
**Base:** `devin/p32-12-dossier-document-adapters` (stacked on PR #168 — merge this after #168) ·
**Run:** `implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/173_P32.13__immutable-releases-and-records.md live_verification=false` ·
**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/173_P32.13__immutable-releases-and-records.md` (manifest row 173)

## What this does

Builds the immutable release contract the public product cites against —
**offline tooling only**: nothing is deployed, staged to a bucket, or exposed;
publication stays with GATE-G3 (`D-R10-PUBLISH-1` OPEN).

### Two-stage release identity (SIG-FIND-001) — `exports.release`

- **`publication_id` (`p-<64 hex>`)** — a pure function of the canonical,
  ID-free `sig.publication-descriptor/1`: input export manifest digest, data
  release id, both as-of cuts, ruleset/resolver versions, the
  `publication-eligibility/1` policy version, the `sig.published-record/1`
  projection schema, renderer identity+revision, and per-compartment
  projection roots hashed over **URL-free, publication-id-free** record
  documents (`exports.published_record` — the record is projected first, then
  *bound* to the namespace). Identical inputs reproduce the namespace **and**
  the emitted bytes; any parser/policy/projection/renderer/input change mints
  a different namespace.
- **`manifest_sha256`** — a separate post-render digest over the
  `sig.release-integrity/1` manifest listing every artifact's (path, media
  type, compartment, licence, bytes, sha256). It is never embedded in an
  artifact it covers — the hash graph is acyclic (artifacts → manifest →
  digest → catalog entry → latest pointer).
- **Same namespace, different bytes → refused.** Re-activation with identical
  bytes is an idempotent no-op; `validate_release` re-hashes the whole tree
  plus per-compartment `records.index.jsonl` completeness (every emitted
  record exactly once) before staging — the latest pointer never moves on a
  partial release.

### Specific record routes (SIG-FIND-002)

`/r/<pub>/c/<compartment>/entity/<type>/<id>.json` + no-JS `index.html` with
`#claim-…` anchors and evidence links, `/r/<pub>/c/<comp>/evidence/<id>/`,
released dossier overviews, per-compartment browse + jurisdiction indexes,
`/releases/` catalog and `/releases/<pub>/` landings — all static, all
zero-JS. Routes are enumerated from the compartment projection, never a
capped index: measured **236,994 records → 475,112 files**.

- **`record_claims` export artifact** (`exports.spine_export`) — per-
  compartment `<comp>/record_claims.jsonl` carrying claim anchors +
  evidence bindings (claim → capture → artifact), sliced by the claim's OWN
  licence compartment; the new `db.artifact_eligible_sql` is the SQL twin of
  the one P32.5 `access_decision` gating the artifact side.
- **Honest states, never invented content** — unavailable vs withdrawn are
  distinct (`sig.tombstone/1` + a no-JS tombstone page carrying only safe
  fields: reason category, authority, decided date, policy version).
- **Latest convenience URLs are not citations** — `/entity/<type>/<id>/`
  stubs say so on the page; `Citation.astro` emits the immutable release
  permalink as the citation-grade form and labels the belief-pinned query
  URL the legacy selector.
- **Legacy historical selectors resolve honestly** — `release resolve` maps
  `?as_of_world=&as_of_belief=&ruleset=` through `sig.compat-index/1` to a
  real activated release, or `invalid`/`unavailable`/`ambiguous`; an
  `unavailable` names what isn't published — never an unchanged page
  labelled historical.

### Release tooling + the access-time withdrawal barrier

`sig-exports release {build,validate,activate,rollback,withdraw,
apply-withdrawals,resolve,check-access,measure}` — the atomic latest pointer
flips via write-then-`os.replace`; rollback re-points to any earlier
activated release **and re-applies the CURRENT withdrawal registry**, so a
withhold recorded under R2 denies under an R1 rollback. Rollback to a
namespace that is itself under a denying release-level disposition is
refused — "latest" never retargets at a wholly-denied tree.

`sig-ops release-serve {apply,check}` (`ops.release_serving`, +
`ops/web/nginx.conf`) applies the same `policy.eligibility` rule to the
staged tree and regenerates `conf/withdrawn_routes.conf` — nginx `location =`
exact-match `return 410` rules that match **before** any `/r/` prefix
location, i.e. before origin file or CDN access. Withdrawals deny whole:
entity → its routes in every compartment; claim → every record carrying it;
release artifact → the whole namespace; `artifact_eligible_sql` → the
exported evidence bindings.

## Acceptance-criteria evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Identical inputs → identical namespace + bytes; input changes → new identity; different bytes under a namespace refused | `test_build_is_deterministic`, `test_descriptor_inputs_change_publication_id`, `test_reactivation_with_different_bytes_refused`, `test_reactivation_with_identical_bytes_is_idempotent` |
| Cited record beyond the 500 slice resolves exact released content offline/no-JS; invalid selectors never return an unchanged "historical" page | `test_record_beyond_500_slice_resolves`, `test_record_html_has_no_scripts_and_links_latest_as_convenience`, `test_resolve_selector_variants`, `test_resolve_ambiguous_when_two_releases_share_the_triple` |
| Incomplete compartment/index fails staging; rollback + tombstone deterministic; measured cost over full corpus | `test_validate_and_activate_fail_on_missing_record`, `test_validate_fails_on_undeclared_artifact`, `test_validate_fails_on_index_digest_mismatch`, `test_withdrawal_tombstones_deterministic`, `test_apply_is_deterministic` (ops), `test_measure_build_reports_cost` + `docs/build/reports/p32.13-release-generation.md` (real corpus) |
| Acyclic digest never embedded in a covered artifact; withdrawal barrier before origin/CDN | `test_integrity_manifest_is_external_and_acyclic`, `test_apply_writes_tombstones_and_deny_map` (ops), `test_withdrawal_denies_under_rollback`, `test_release_withdrawal_denies_the_whole_namespace`, `test_route_access_denies_routes_under_a_withdrawn_release`, `test_route_access_denies_record_carrying_a_denied_claim`, `test_rollback_to_a_withdrawn_release_is_refused` |
| Verification green; ids stamped; ADR for new decisions | this PR + ADR-132 + `COVERAGE_MATRIX` SIG-FIND-001/002 → MET |

## Not done (explicitly out of scope)

- No deploy, bucket push, DNS/CDN or live exposure — `D-R10-PUBLISH-1` OPEN,
  GATE-G3 owns it; the nginx change is committed config for the staging
  posture, not a deployed one.
- No source/rights flips, no human labels, no spine writes — the export path
  is read-only; `record_claims` reuses the P32.5 selector verbatim.
- Full-corpus search (`P32.14`) consumes these routes; this ticket ships the
  immutable namespaces it searches over.
